issues.legal_issue: A litigant seeking judicial relief must disclose material facts fully and may be denied relief for concealing facts that bear on the dispute.
material_facts: After the land had been declared vested in the State, the company entered into a lease agreement for the excess land and acknowledged in that agreement that the purchases were contrary to the statutory restriction, void, and had caused the land to vest in the State.
The company did not disclose the lease agreement or its contents to the revisional authority, the High Court, or the Supreme Court while challenging the vesting orders.
The company obtained interim orders while its challenge proceeded without disclosure of the lease.
issues.conclusion: The company had not approached the courts with clean hands and was not entitled to relief; the appeal was dismissed and costs were imposed.
issues.legal_principle: A party seeking equitable or other judicial relief has a duty to disclose all material facts and not suppress facts within its knowledge. A court may refuse relief on that ground without proceeding to the merits. The Court relied on R. v. Kensington Income Tax Commissioner (1917) 1 KB 486; State of Haryana v. Karnal Distillery Co. Ltd. (1977) 2 SCC 431; S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu v. Jagannath (1994) 1 SCC 1; Prestige Lights Ltd. v. State Bank of India (2007) 8 SCC 449; K.D. Sharma v. Steel Authority of India Ltd. (2008) 12 SCC 481; Hari Narain v. Badri Das, AIR 1963 SC 1558; and Dalip Singh v. State of U.P. (decided 3 December 2009).

predicates.appeal_seeking_relief: A litigant appeals or otherwise seeks judicial relief concerning an adverse decision.
predicates.material_fact_known_to_litigant: The litigant knows a fact that bears materially on the dispute and the relief sought.
predicates.material_fact_withheld_from_court: The litigant does not disclose that material fact to the court hearing the claim.

issues.definition: When a litigant seeking relief knows and withholds a fact material to the dispute, the court may deny relief and impose costs.

issues.legal_issue: A party that admitted the relevant facts and did not seek an opportunity to prove otherwise cannot establish that the decision-maker denied it a reasonable hearing.
material_facts: In its written statements, the company admitted that it had purchased land exceeding the permitted area without waiting for government permission, believing permission would be granted, and stated that it had no objection to legal action concerning the excess land.
The company did not ask the Collector for permission to lead evidence that the purchases complied with the law.
Before the revisional authority and the High Court, the company did not complain that it had been denied a reasonable or effective hearing.
issues.conclusion: The company could not successfully contend that the Collector had violated the rule of audi alteram partem.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the hearing complaint against the company's admissions, its failure to seek an opportunity to produce evidence, and its failure to raise the complaint before the revisional authority or the High Court. It found no basis on those facts to hold that the Collector had denied a reasonable hearing.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_land_transfer_order and party_admitted_material_facts and party_did_not_seek_evidence and party_did_not_raise_hearing_complaint_earlier

predicates.appeal_challenging_land_transfer_order: A party appeals an order concerning the validity or consequences of a land transfer.
predicates.party_admitted_material_facts: The party admitted facts relevant to whether the transfer complied with the applicable restriction.
predicates.party_did_not_seek_evidence: The party did not ask the original decision-maker for an opportunity to produce evidence on the disputed issue.
predicates.party_did_not_raise_hearing_complaint_ea: The party did not complain of inadequate opportunity before the subsequent reviewing authorities.

issues.definition: In an appeal about a land transfer, a party's admissions, failure to seek evidence, and failure to raise a hearing complaint earlier mean that denial of a reasonable hearing is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory restriction on land transfers to a person includes transfers to a company where the governing general-interpretation law includes companies within that term.
material_facts: A company purchased land exceeding the statutory limit without first obtaining permission.
The company argued that the restriction applied only to natural persons and that the holdings of its directors should be treated separately.
No evidence showed that the land had been purchased in the names of the directors rather than in the company's name.
The company was not shown to qualify for an exception permitting excess land to be transferred.
issues.conclusion: The statutory term “person” included a company, and the restriction applied to the company's purchase; the company's holdings could not be divided among its directors on the evidence presented.
issues.legal_principle: Section 154(1) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act restricts transfers to a person that would cause the transferee's relevant holding to exceed the prescribed limit; section 154(2) provides specified exceptions. Sections 3(1) and 4(33) of the U.P. General Clauses Act, 1904 make “person” include a company or association of individuals unless the context requires otherwise. The Court applied the contextual approach recognized in Poppatlal Shah v. State of Madras, AIR 1953 SC 274; S.K. Gupta v. K.P. Jain (1979) 3 SCC 54; Reserve Bank of India v. Peerless General Finance and Investment Co. Ltd. (1987) 1 SCC 424; and Central Bank of India v. State of Kerala (2009) 4 SCC 94. It also relied on the treatment of inclusive definitions in Dilworth v. Commissioner of Stamps (1899) AC 99, State of Bombay v. Hospital Mazdoor Sabha, AIR 1960 SC 610, and CIT v. Taj Mahal Hotel (1971) 3 SCC 550, and on Hasmukhlal Dahayabhai v. State of Gujarat (1976) 4 SCC 100 and Ramanlal Bhailal Patel v. State of Gujarat (2008) 5 SCC 449. The interpretation accords with the legislation's social-justice purpose and Articles 38 and 39 of the Constitution.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_land_transfer and transferee_is_company and company_holding_exceeds_limit and no_applicable_exception

predicates.appeal_concerning_land_transfer: A party appeals a decision about whether a land transfer is permitted under a statutory landholding restriction.
predicates.transferee_is_company: The land was transferred to a company rather than to individuals in their separate capacities.
predicates.company_holding_exceeds_limit: The company's landholding after the transfer exceeded the applicable statutory limit.
predicates.no_applicable_exception: The company did not establish that an exception to the restriction applied.

issues.definition: When a company receives a transfer that takes its holding over the limit and no exception applies, it is treated as a person subject to the restriction.

issues.legal_issue: A land transfer made contrary to the statutory restriction is void and causes the transferred land to vest in the State.
material_facts: The company purchased land exceeding the statutory limit without obtaining the required permission.
The company did not establish that the transfer fell within an exception to the restriction.
The company acknowledged in its lease agreement that the transfers were contrary to the restriction and that the excess land had vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: The transfers of land in excess of the permitted limit were void, and the excess land vested in the State from the date of transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 154(1) and 154(2) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act impose the transfer restriction and provide specified exceptions. Section 166 makes a transfer contrary to the Act void. Section 167(1)(a) provides that the subject matter of a void transfer vests in the State free from encumbrances from the date of transfer, and section 167(2) authorizes the Collector to take possession and direct eviction. The Court also described the later-added section 154(3) as requiring prior approval for excess transfers while permitting post facto approval in the circumstances specified there.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_land_transfer and land_transfer_exceeds_limit and required_permission_absent and no_applicable_exception

predicates.appeal_concerning_land_transfer: A party appeals a decision about the validity or consequences of a land transfer.
predicates.land_transfer_exceeds_limit: The transfer caused the transferee's relevant holding to exceed the statutory limit.
predicates.required_permission_absent: The required government permission or approval was not obtained.
predicates.no_applicable_exception: The transfer did not qualify for an applicable statutory exception.

issues.definition: If a transfer exceeds the limit, required permission is absent, and no exception applies, the excess transfer is void and the land vests in the State.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a corporate representative's authority to admit an unlawful land purchase may fail where the representative was authorized to take necessary land-transfer actions and the company's later conduct confirmed the admission.
material_facts: The company's board authorized its general manager, among others, to negotiate and finalize land purchases, sign documents for acquisition or transfer, and do other acts considered proper in carrying out those duties.
The general manager filed a written statement admitting that the company had purchased land without waiting for permission and stating that legal action could be taken concerning the excess land.

The company later executed a lease agreement through a director and a general manager, expressly acknowledging that the excess land had been acquired contrary to the restriction and had vested in the State.
The company did not disclose that lease agreement to the reviewing authorities or the courts during its challenge.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge to the general manager's authority and found no fault in the Collector's reliance on the company's written statement.
issues.legal_principle: The scope of the board's authorization, considered together with the company's later express admission in a lease signed by its director and general manager, undermined the claim that the general manager had acted beyond his authority. The Court therefore found no basis to fault the Collector for relying on the written statement.

predicates.appeal_challenging_land_transfer_order: A party appeals an order that relied on an admission made in proceedings about a land transfer.
predicates.representative_authorized_for_land_trans: The company authorized the representative to take actions necessary for acquiring or transferring land.
predicates.company_later_confirmed_admission_throug: The company later acknowledged the same material facts through signatories authorized to act for it.

issues.definition: When an authorized land-transfer representative makes an admission that the company later confirms through authorized signatories, the admission is not set aside for lack of authority.

issues.legal_issue: A request for post facto approval of an excess land transfer may be refused where the applicant has suppressed material facts and has not laid a factual foundation for the request.
material_facts: The company asked the Court to direct the State to grant post facto approval for its excess purchase under a later-added statutory provision.
The company had concealed the lease agreement that acknowledged the excess transfers were unlawful and that the land had vested in the State.
The company provided no factual foundation for its request for post facto approval.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain or grant the request for post facto approval.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 154(3) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act permits the State, on an application, to grant post facto approval in the circumstances specified by that provision. The Court refused to entertain this request because the company had not approached the Court with clean hands and had supplied no factual foundation for the relief.

predicates.appeal_seeking_post_facto_land_approval: A party asks a reviewing court to secure later government approval for an excess land transfer.
predicates.material_fact_withheld_from_court: The party concealed from the court a fact material to its request or the underlying transfer.
predicates.factual_foundation_absent: The party did not provide facts supporting the requested approval.

issues.definition: A request for later approval of an excess land transfer is not entertained when the applicant conceals a material fact and provides no factual support for the request.

issues.legal_issue: The State must not renew a lease that gives temporary legitimacy to possession of land that vested in it following a void transfer.
material_facts: The company had acquired land in excess of the statutory limit, and the excess land had vested in the State.
The State subsequently leased the excess land to the company for a fixed term.
The Court considered that granting the lease frustrated the purpose of the land-reform legislation and the vesting order.
issues.conclusion: The State was directed not to renew the lease when its term ended and to deal with the excess land in accordance with the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 154, 166, and 167 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act restrict excess transfers, make contravening transfers void, and provide for vesting in the State. The Court reasoned that leasing the vested land back to the transferee frustrated the legislation's purpose and directed that the lease not be renewed.

predicates.land_vested_in_state_after_void_transfer: The land vested in the State as a consequence of a void transfer.
predicates.state_leased_vested_land_to_transferee: The State granted the former transferee a lease of the vested land.

issues.definition: When the State leases to a former transferee land that vested in it after a void transfer, the lease must not be renewed.
